1. What Was Built

Starting from iML1515 (the most complete E. coli GEM, with 1515 genes), three complete EPS biosynthetic routes were added so the model can measure EPS secretion as a real, quantifiable output. Before this work, EPS flux in the model was zero — the cell had enzymes for EPS precursors but no way to route carbon all the way to a secreted polymer.

PathwayEPS ProductNew reactions addedStatus
Cellulose (bcsA)β-1,4-glucose polymer CELSYNTH, CELLULOSEt, EX_cellulose_e 3 NEW
Colanic acid (Wca)Glc + Gal + GlcA + 2×Fuc + pyruvate COLASYNTH, COLAIDt, EX_colacid_e 3 NEW
PNAG (pgaC)Poly-β-1,6-GlcNAc PUACGAMex, EX_puacgam_e 2 NEW 2 already in model

2. The Three EPS Pathways — Stoichiometry

Cellulose (bcsA) — CELSYNTH

udpg_c + 0.001 cdigmp_c → cellulose_c + udp_c

UDP-glucose is the carbon donor. c-di-GMP (made by ydaM/DGUNC) is required as a small cofactor, connecting the biofilm regulatory signal to synthesis. Knocking out yahA/gmr (CDGUNPD/LDGUNPD) forces all c-di-GMP through bcsA.

Colanic Acid (Wca) — COLASYNTH

udcpgl_c + udpgal_c + udpglcur_c + 2×gdpfuc_c + pep_c → colacid_c + udcpp_c + 2×udp_c + 2×gdp_c + pi_c

Uses udcpgl_c — the product of wcaJ (UDPGPT, already in iML1515) — as the glucose starter on the undecaprenyl carrier. Then adds galactose, glucuronate, two fucose, and a pyruvate modification from PEP. All precursors already existed in iML1515. The undecaprenyl carrier (udcpp_c) is recycled back for wcaJ to reuse.

PNAG (pgaC) — largely already in iML1515

uacgam_c → puacgam_c + udp_c (PUACGAMS in reverse)
puacgam_c → puacgam_p (PUACGAMtr — already in model)
puacgam_p → puacgam_e → [secreted] (PUACGAMex + EX_puacgam_e — new)

The synthesis and periplasmic transport were already in iML1515. Only the extracellular export step needed to be added.

4. Before vs After — Impact of Adding Each Pathway

Each model version was run under all 6 conditions at 90% max growth.

Figure 2. EPS flux (mmol/gDW/h) per condition for each model version. Grey = no EPS pathway (baseline = 0). Each coloured group shows the progressive gain from adding pathways. Orange = all three pathways combined.

Progression summary (combined_EPS condition):
No pathway → 0 mmol/gDW/h
+ Cellulose only → 16.4 mmol/gDW/h
+ Colanic acid only → 3.1 mmol/gDW/h
+ PNAG only → 0.2 mmol/gDW/h (N-limited — PNAG is N-containing, restricted by low NH₄⁺)
All three → 19.7 mmol/gDW/h total

6. Pathway Contributions per Condition

Figure 3. Left: EPS flux in mmol/gDW/h stacked by pathway. Right: EPS per cell in fg/cell/h stacked by pathway. Cellulose dominates under N-limitation and combined conditions. PNAG drops under N-limitation because its monomer (UDP-GlcNAc) contains nitrogen.

7. Key Biological Insights

Cellulose dominates total EPS in almost all conditions.
Under combined_EPS (high glucose + N-limited + c-di-GMP on), cellulose accounts for 16.4 of the 19.7 mmol/gDW/h total (~83%). Colanic acid contributes ~15% and PNAG ~2%. This matches literature: cellulose is the major matrix component in E. coli biofilms.
PNAG is suppressed by nitrogen limitation — an emergent model result.
PNAG is poly-GlcNAc. UDP-GlcNAc contains nitrogen (the N-acetyl group). Under N-limitation, the model correctly reduces PNAG production because nitrogen is scarce and the cell prioritises protein/growth over N-containing EPS. This was not explicitly programmed — it emerged from the metabolic network. Biologically, this is consistent with observations that PNAG production is favoured in nitrogen-replete conditions.
c-di-GMP signal alone is insufficient without carbon surplus.
The EPS_phenotype condition (only c-di-GMP knockouts, standard nutrients) gives the same EPS as baseline. Carbon availability, not just the regulatory switch, limits EPS production. The combined condition (carbon surplus + nitrogen stress + c-di-GMP on) is needed for maximum EPS.
Colanic acid uses wcaJ (already in iML1515) as its first committed step.
The UDPGPT reaction (wcaJ) was a dead-end in the original model. By building COLASYNTH on top of its product (udcpgl_c), that dead-end is now productive. The undecaprenyl carrier (udcpp_c) is recycled, which is also biologically correct.

These are upper bound predictions. FBA finds the theoretical maximum — real cells will produce less due to regulatory delays, costs not captured in the model, and cellular maintenance requirements. Use these values to rank conditions and estimate order of magnitude, not as absolute quantitative predictions.

10. Next Steps

  1. Run cells 33–37 in the notebook (model v3 section) to regenerate all figures in a live Jupyter session.
  2. Gene knockout screen: knock out each EPS gene one at a time and measure which ones most reduce EPS flux — identifies rate-limiting targets for engineering.
  3. Production envelope for Wca and PNAG — the envelopes in Figure 4 are for cellulose only. Running them for all three would show which pathway has the best growth-EPS trade-off.
  4. Experimental validation: the combined_EPS condition (~1.5 ng EPS/cell/h) predicts high glucose (20 mM) + low ammonium (2 mM) as the most productive media. This is a direct experimental hypothesis to test.
  5. Production envelope for colanic acid: add the Wca pathway envelope to Figure 4 to compare the growth-EPS trade-off between cellulose and colanic acid.
